problem: Measures EIP-7702 use across 7 chains: >63% of 3.66M authorizations tied to malicious EOA-targeted attacks; $2.36M losses, $10.14M exposed
trust_assumption: Users and wallets decide what to authorize
ibs_relation: Evidence for C2 default-deny of delegation and C4 code-at-EOA tripwire; consumer phishing, not custodial orchestration
gap: Does not address custodial signers whose orchestration requests delegations

problem: Shows one phished authorization tuple gives persistent full control; three trigger pathways; first cross-chain usage measurement; protocol-level defenses
trust_assumption: Wallet shows the authorization faithfully; user judges it
ibs_relation: Prior art for the delegation threat; complements C2 (deny 7702 by default)
gap: Consumer phishing; no institutional signing policy or post-sign containment

problem: Reference frame for 181 DeFi incidents; 56% of attacks non-atomic, leaving a rescue window
ibs_relation: Supports C4 premise (time to respond exists); DeFi protocols, not custodial signing
gap: Custodial key/signing-path incidents out of scope

problem: Systematizes 31 bridge attacks (2021-2023) into 10 vulnerability types; defenses and open problems
ibs_relation: Context for U2 incidents and validator-key compromise; C1 analogue = deposit-evidence binding
gap: Off-chain signer compromise treated as key management, not intent binding

problem: Analyzes 36 Bitcoin exchange breaches with a CTI standard; most due to lax security
ibs_relation: Baseline empirical work on exchange breaches (pre-2020)
gap: Stops before account-abstraction era and signing-request manipulation

problem: Extended breach analysis, security posture of surviving exchanges, laundering of stolen BTC
ibs_relation: Baseline empirical work; laundering context for S4
gap: Bitcoin-only; no signing-path analysis

problem: Four practical key-extraction attacks on threshold-ECDSA (GG18/GG20, Lindell17) implementations used by MPC wallets
ibs_relation: Shows MPC protects the key, not the decision to sign; IBS is orthogonal (sits before the signer)
gap: Does not address an honest MPC quorum signing a malicious but valid request

problem: Real-time anomaly detection for DeFi protocols: 109/115 incidents detected within block time, 0.16% FP
trust_assumption: Protocol behaviour models learned from history
post_sign_containment: yes (detection; prevention if wired to pause)
ibs_relation: Closest academic analogue to C4 for protocols; IBS's watcher targets custodial treasury flows and reconciles against an intent ledger
gap: Protocol contracts, not custodial hot wallets; no intent ledger

problem: Mempool fuzzer finds new asymmetric-DoS bugs in six clients including Besu
ibs_relation: Closest prior work to our client mempool-semantics finding (E8); positions sim-to-real gap
gap: DoS focus; does not study how mempool admission changes theft outcomes

problem: Evaluates 53 Ethereum wallets against address poisoning; few warn users
ibs_relation: Display-integrity evidence; consumer wallets
gap: Not custodial; no policy or containment

problem: Six recurring flaws in audited ERC-4337 smart accounts (access control, signature binding, paymasters)
ibs_relation: Shows programmable accounts move risk into account code; relevant if IBS is enforced on-chain
gap: Grey literature; implementation flaws, not signing-path compromise

problem: BitForge: GG18/GG20 Paillier-key flaw allows full key extraction (CVE-2023-33241); many wallets affected
ibs_relation: Same point as makriyannis2023mpcattacks from the vendor side
gap: Grey literature

problem: Wallet design taxonomy; multi-layer attack framework; 84 wallet incidents 2012-2024 ($5.4B); precautionary vs remedial defenses
trust_assumption: Varies by wallet type; custodial wallets trust the operator's infrastructure
ibs_relation: Evidence base for RQ1; public incident dataset is a second source for our catalog cross-check
gap: Classifies wallet types, not the custodial signing pipeline; no evaluation of defenses against orchestration compromise

problem: Covenants restrict how outputs can be spent; vaults force a publicly visible delay so a stolen key can be countered by a recovery key
trust_assumption: Recovery key stays uncompromised; owner watches the chain during the delay
ibs_relation: Closest prior art for C3+C4: bounded, delayed exposure plus a recovery path
gap: Needs a Bitcoin consensus change; no notion of operation intent; delay applies to every spend, so it suits cold storage, not hot-wallet throughput

problem: Policy-based signatures: a key can only sign messages that satisfy an authority-set policy, and signatures hide the policy
trust_assumption: Authority issuing policy keys is honest; policy fixed at key issuance
ibs_relation: Cryptographic analogue of C2 (deny-by-default policy enforced at signing)
gap: Policy is static per key, not tied to a per-operation intent; non-standard verification, so not usable for ECDSA accounts on-chain

problem: Policy-compliant signatures: a signature is valid only if a global policy over sender and receiver attributes is satisfied
trust_assumption: Central authority sets the policy and issues keys
ibs_relation: Cryptographic analogue of C2 with receiver-aware policy (e.g. who may pay whom)
gap: Same as PBS: static policy, custom verification; no intent binding or containment

problem: First security study of Ethereum txpool designs; low-cost DoS by flawed admission control in all known clients
ibs_relation: Shows txpool admission rules differ by client and matter for security; context for limitation E8
gap: Studies DoS, not how queued underfunded transactions change loss outcomes in a theft

problem: Phishing contracts that look benign under wallet transaction simulation and behave differently on-chain; SimGuard detector; >4,000 contracts, >5,700 victims, ~$3.48M
ibs_relation: Shows a pre-sign preview can be gamed; supports checking the signed operation against intent (C1) and reconciling outcomes after execution (C4)
gap: Consumer wallets; no custodial policy or post-execution containment

problem: Datalog rules model expected cross-chain behaviour and flag anomalies; finds the Ronin and Nomad attack transactions
trust_assumption: Bridge events and rules are complete; detection is after the fact
evaluation: incident analysis (replay of Ronin and Nomad data)
ibs_relation: Prior art for rule-based reconciliation in C4
gap: Detection only; validator-key compromise (Ronin) is found after the loss

problem: End-to-end balance invariant (outflow = inflow - costs) flags every known bridge attack in their data; in-line enforcement via announce-then-execute
trust_assumption: Accounting data on both chains is correct and timely
independent_intent: partial (inflow on the source chain acts as an independent record)
post_sign_containment: yes (in-line audit can block unbalanced withdrawals)
ibs_relation: Strongest prior art for C4 as accounting reconciliation; reported to have inspired a deployed system (Bascule)
gap: Bridges only; an exchange hot wallet has no on-chain inflow record matching each withdrawal, so the invariant needs an off-chain intent ledger

problem: Systematic review and empirical comparison of blockchain simulators
ibs_relation: Methodological context for our simulator plus real-client (Besu) design
gap: Simulators target consensus/network performance, not transaction-level security outcomes

problem: Systematic mapping of blockchain simulators: features, inputs, validated metrics; none covers the full range
ibs_relation: Context for E7 (one client) and the sim-to-real comparison
gap: Same focus as above

problem: New transaction type that lets an EOA set delegated code via signed authorization tuples
trust_assumption: Holder of the EOA key signs authorizations knowingly
ibs_relation: Defines the attack surface for A3 and the C2/C4 rules on delegation
gap: Standard itself; security depends on wallets and policy

problem: Account abstraction through UserOperations, bundlers and an EntryPoint contract, without consensus changes
ibs_relation: Context: smart accounts move policy into validation code
gap: Policy in validation code is only as good as what it can see

problem: Interfaces for modular smart accounts: validators, executors, hooks
trust_assumption: Installed modules are correct and not replaced
post_sign_containment: partial (hooks can check before and after execution)
ibs_relation: Hooks are a possible on-chain enforcement point for C2/C3
gap: Module installation is itself a privileged signing action

problem: Standard order format for cross-chain intents filled by solvers
ibs_relation: Terminology only: 'intent' here is a solver-filled order, not an independently authored operation record
gap: Different problem (execution outsourcing)

problem: JSON descriptors so wallets can show contract calls and typed messages in human-readable form (clear signing)
trust_assumption: Descriptor registry, external data sources (token metadata, ENS) and the device display
independent_intent: no (the human compares the display with their own belief)
ibs_relation: Prior art and complement for C1: makes the payload readable at the signer; its own security section names front-end/CDN compromise and registry poisoning, and lists binding frontends to verified manifests as future work
gap: Readable is not the same as intended: nothing checks the call against an intent recorded elsewhere

problem: Protocol-level circuit breaker: delay or revert token outflows once a rate threshold is exceeded
trust_assumption: Thresholds are set well; the operator can't be the attacker
ibs_relation: Prior art for C3 exposure budgets enforced on-chain
gap: DeFi protocol scope; a third-party audit (Zellic) reports complexity and a griefing path; never standardized

problem: Industry control standard for key material: generation, storage, usage (incl. spend verification, multi-signer use), compromise policy, audit logs
independent_intent: partial (spend verification; text still to be read)
ibs_relation: Standards baseline; IBS controls should map onto CCSS aspect 1.05
gap: Process controls; does not specify an independent machine-checkable intent or automatic containment

problem: Technical reconstruction of Bybit: injected Safe{Wallet} UI code sent altered data to hardware wallets; after the attack the Safe gateway began checking that proposal hash and signature match
ibs_relation: Evidence that the proposal-to-signature binding was missing at the orchestration layer (C1 gap)
gap: Single incident; vendor analysis

problem: Reviews 2022-2023 bridge hacks and exploited weaknesses; notes several were caused by poor IT practice rather than on-chain code
ibs_relation: Evidence that bridge losses often come from the operational signing path (U2/U3 scope)
gap: Review only; no defense evaluation

problem: Breaks bridges into components and reviews exploits by component
ibs_relation: Bridge-component vocabulary for U2 incidents
gap: Pre-2023 incidents; no evaluation

problem: Survival analysis of 40 Bitcoin exchanges: 18 closed, 9 breached; high-volume exchanges close less but are breached more
ibs_relation: Foundational evidence that exchange custody is the dominant user risk
gap: Early era; no signing-path detail

problem: Revisits exchange closure risk with 80 exchanges (2010-2015) and quarterly indicators
ibs_relation: Longitudinal baseline for RQ1
gap: Closure risk, not theft mechanics

problem: Tamarin model of the EIP-7702 delegation lifecycle composed with the ERC-4337 EntryPoint; ten machine-checked attack patterns; checks mitigations
trust_assumption: Symbolic model matches client and contract behaviour
ibs_relation: Method we can reuse to formally check C2 delegation rules; independent confirmation of the 7702 attack surface behind A3
gap: Account-level; no custodial orchestration or containment

problem: Identifies and profiles on-chain wallet contracts on Ethereum; groups them into six types (limits, approvals, multisig, recovery)
ibs_relation: Shows which on-chain policy features (daily limits, approvals) wallets actually ship: C3-like budgets exist on-chain
gap: Pre-2021 data; no attack evaluation

problem: Explains ERC-4337 account abstraction and qualitatively assesses its security effect
ibs_relation: Background for RQ5
gap: Qualitative only

problem: PRISMA-ScR review building a dataset of 220 exchange incidents (80 CEX, 140 DEX, 2009-2024, $8.494B); classifies attack vectors; discusses post-quantum risk
ibs_relation: Candidate second source for our catalog cross-check (CEX incidents)
gap: Different inclusion rules and loss sources from ours; per-incident evidence must be checked
